title: Bernie Moreno Calls Abdul El-Sayed Most Extreme Candidate in 2026 Midterms
text:
Sen. Bernie Moreno told Breitbart News that Michigan Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed is the most extreme socialist in the 2026 midterms, citing his jihadist credentials.
Sen. Bernie Moreno (R-OH) said on Thursday that Michigan Democrat Senate candidate Abdulrahman Mohamed El-Sayed is the most extreme candidate in the 2026 midterms, citing what he described as El-Sayed's jihadist credentials. Moreno made the remarks during a Breitbart News event in response to a question from a participant named Barry M. about the most extreme socialist candidate running.
Moreno Ranks El-Sayed as Most Extreme
When asked who the most extreme socialist candidate in the 2026 midterms is, Moreno compared the question to asking who is the tallest midget, calling it a tough choice. He then said that on sheer jihadist credentials, the answer would have to be Abdul El-Sayed.
Moreno described El-Sayed as a wolf in sheep's clothing. He said El-Sayed appears on Fox News and deflects every question, giving the example of being asked whether he wanted America to suffer during 9/11 and responding that people cannot afford groceries. Moreno said that is not the question that was asked and called El-Sayed the most dangerous one.
Comparison to Mamdani and Car Business Warning
Moreno went on to compare El-Sayed to a Mamdani situation, referring to the Muslim socialist New York City mayor. He also drew on his background in the car business, saying he grew up in the car business and remembers it in the 1980s and 1990s. He added that the guys you have to watch out for are the slick ones.
El-Sayed has said he is not a socialist, though he is running on a platform backed by socialist lawmakers Sen. Bernie Sanders (I-VT), Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez (D-NY), and Rep. Rashida Tlaib (D-MI). He has also campaigned with far-left streamer Hasan Piker.
Homeland Security Concerns Raised in Senate Hearing
A Senate counterterrorism expert warned in August at a Senate Judiciary Subcommittee hearing on Muslim Brotherhood threats in the U.S. that El-Sayed's candidacy raises homeland security concerns. According to Fox News, the expert cited family ties to Muslim Brotherhood-linked groups and connections to a Midwest voter-engagement organization the expert said is tied to the Council on American-Islamic Relations (CAIR).
The hearing focused on Muslim Brotherhood threats in the United States. The expert's warning added to the scrutiny of El-Sayed's candidacy ahead of the 2026 midterms.
The Breitbart Fight Club roundtable event where Moreno spoke allows participants to interact live with national leaders and ask questions directly. Moreno's comments come as the 2026 midterm races draw increasing attention, with Michigan's Senate contest emerging as a focal point of debate over political extremism and national security.
